result.text:
I added all three features: repeated commands, sonar and guarded runs. All 53 tests pass with `gradle test`: the 16 original tests, unchanged, plus 37 new ones.

## Design (`src/main/java/surveycrawler`)
- **Sonar:** `Sonar` is an interface with `groundTypeAt(Point)`. `SurveyCrawler.atFacingWith(position, facing, sonar[, random])` builds a crawler with a sonar. The old `atFacing` still works and uses `FirmSandOnlySonar`.
- **Ground types:** `FirmSand`, `Silt` and `Boulder` are subclasses of `GroundType`, and each one decides what happens when the crawler moves onto it or turns on it. A boulder raises an exception, silt slides the crawler, and firm sand moves it normally. There is no ground-type `if` in the crawler. All moves go through a single method, `moveTowards(direction)`, which asks the sonar about the destination cell before moving.
- **Sliding on silt:** the crawler slides `random.nextInt(10) + 1` cells in the direction it was going, so from `(1,2)` it can end anywhere from `(1,3)` to `(1,12)`. Retreating onto silt slides it backwards. The `Random` is passed in so tests can control it.
- **Guarded runs:** the crawler has a run state, either `UnguardedRun` or `GuardedRun`. `GuardedRun` does four things:
  - It records each change of position or facing (`PositionChange`, `FacingChange`).
  - When an error happens, it undoes those changes in reverse order and rethrows the original exception.
  - It rejects a `(` inside a guarded run, silt, and a sequence that ends before the `)`.
  
  `UnguardedRun` records nothing, and a `)` there is an error.
- **Repetition:** a digit repeats the command right before it digit + 2 more times, but only if that command is `a`, `t`, `h` or `g`. Otherwise the digit is an invalid command.

## Cases the requirements didn't cover, and what I chose
- **Digit misuse:** a digit at the start (`"3a"`), two digits in a row (`"a10"`), or a digit after `(`, `)` or an invalid command raises "Invalid command".
- **`)` without a `(`:** raises its own error. Commands before it have already run, as with invalid commands today.
- **Sliding into a boulder:** the crawler stops in the cell before the boulder, with no exception, since the move onto the silt itself was allowed.
- **Silt during a guarded run:** the check happens before the crawler moves, so the random slide never happens. The end result is the same as moving and then undoing.
- **Undo never uses the sonar:** undoing a move just applies the reverse change to position or facing. Otherwise backing over silt would slide the crawler again (test 53).
- **Several guarded runs in one sequence:** a failure only undoes the guarded run that failed; commands before it and earlier finished guarded runs stay done (tests 42 and 47).
- **After a failed or unfinished guarded run:** the crawler goes back to unguarded, so the next `process` call behaves normally (tests 51 and 52).
- **Error messages:** each new error has its own description method, like the existing `invalidCommandErrorDescription()`.

The tests use two test-only helpers in `src/test/java/surveycrawler`: `SimulatedSonar`, a map of positions to ground types, and `FixedRandom`. One test also uses a real `Random` to check that the crawler always stops within the 10-cell limit.
